reviews.review:
As you can see, I have so, so many hours on this game. I love it. But don't get attached, because more awful monetization seems to be coming.

Arma 3 is a very unique game. It's got its campaigns, but that's not where it shines. Arma 3 is military D&D. The moddability, sophisticated mission editor, and nearly unheard of "Zeus" game master mode lets you build and run unique missions and campaigns that naturally change based on player outcomes: you can expand the base game's story, or storm the beaches of Normandy, or play the Sino-Soviet border conflict, or play the Union Army in the civil war, or join the 501st Legion as it fights alongside Anakin Skywalker. And if you suddenly decide "this Skywalker guy is trouble, we should take him out now," you can do that and the GM can build on it. The possibilities are endless.

The jank is real. It's a Rube Goldburg Machine of a game running on ancient code and it'll fling you into the sky if you drive your truck into a plastic lawn chair. But even today, 13 years later, no other game I know gives you this much freedom to build and play what you want to make.

Which brings us to the problem: monetization. Value extraction, return on investment, en****tification, whatever you want to call it. Up until today, it's been okay. DLCs and such, and they do let you have some limited play with DLC content even without purchasing the DLC, which is very nice. But today they rolled out a subscription. In and of itself, there's nothing horrible about $9 a month for access to all the DLCs, but it's very obvious that this is setting the stage for more aggressive monetization down the road. Arma 4 is coming, and when it arrives I want it to be free of subscriptions, battle passes, FOMO, lootboxes, and all the other predatory practices that the games industry is enamored with. And make no mistake, they will push this as far as they think they can get away with. We've seen it time and time again.

This game is something special. Don't let it join the pile of games that have been ruined by men who stare at spreadsheets all day.
